token_supply.notes: Counts are measured with tokenizer/taksh_code_bpe_v1.json except corpus_v0, whose documented figure is with the obsolete 49,152-vocab tokenizer.

token_supply_disclosure: code supply (1,590,703) is licence-verified in-repo code (M3 MIT/BSD + Apache-2.0 repo snapshot).
general supply (l03 ~19.6M) is English Wikipedia/Gutenberg (CC-BY-SA-3.0 / Public Domain); it is not code.
corpus_v0's 9,993,983-token figure uses the obsolete 49,152-vocab tokenizer; re-encoded equivalent would be ~9-11M tokens.
counting repeated epochs as new data is not done anywhere in this analysis.

mixture_guidance: practical mixture for a code model: aim >= 60% high-quality code tokens, bounded general-text fraction (~20-30%) for instruction following; repetition beyond ~4 epochs of unique data yields strongly diminished returns

dataset_candidate_register.name: BigCode The Stack (v1)
dataset_candidate_register.languages: 358 programming languages incl. Python, JS/TS, Java, C/C++, Go, Rust
dataset_candidate_register.published_size: reported as ~6.4 TB across ~200M repositories' files; filtered release is smaller (reported ~1 TB)
dataset_candidate_register.access: registration + terms acceptance on the Hugging Face hub
dataset_candidate_register.license: BigCode OpenRAIL License (data access); per-file licenses follow the originating repositories (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD/CC0-class filtered variants exist)
dataset_candidate_register.source_code_obligations: copyleft files (GPL/LGPL) in bulk subsets impose source-offer/notice obligations; BigCode provides a license-filtered subset precisely to avoid this
dataset_candidate_register.attribution: per-file origin must be tracked for attribution if redistribution is ever contemplated
dataset_candidate_register.redistribution: not for public redistribution of the corpus itself; derivative models permitted with naming/notice requirements under OpenRAIL variants
dataset_candidate_register.opt_out: opt-out mechanism exists upstream; downstream users inherit a duty to honour removal requests
dataset_candidate_register.commercial_use: BigCode OpenRAIL permits commercial use subject to use restrictions; per-file copyleft can complicate proprietary redistribution
dataset_candidate_register.quality_security: large-scale secret contamination reported; requires credential scanning; near-duplicate heavy; documentation quality uneven
dataset_candidate_register.verdict: STRONG candidate pending legal review; biggest realistic source of Python tokens

dataset_candidate_register.name: BigCode The Stack v2 / StarCoder2 data
dataset_candidate_register.published_size: reported 67.5 TB raw; tokenized code corpora ~2-3T tokens (reported)
dataset_candidate_register.license: BigCode OpenRAIL-M (M = for models); per-file filtering to permissive/public licenses applied by upstream
dataset_candidate_register.source_code_obligations: subset retains only files whose licenses permit codebase inclusion; per-file origin tracking required
dataset_candidate_register.attribution: expected on any redistribution of the corpus; derivative model notices advised
dataset_candidate_register.redistribution: not redistributable as a corpus; model outputs not covered by corpus license
dataset_candidate_register.opt_out: opt-out honoured; users agreed to honour it downstream
dataset_candidate_register.commercial_use: restricted use categories (no large-scale surveillance, no weapons etc.); commercial generally permitted
dataset_candidate_register.quality_security: license-filtered and deduplicated upstream; still needs secret scan + near-dup and benchmark-leakage re-check by us
dataset_candidate_register.verdict: STRONG candidate; best-aligned with this project's filtering discipline

dataset_candidate_register.name: CodeSearchNet (GitHub-derived)
dataset_candidate_register.languages: Go, Java, JavaScript, PHP, Python, Ruby
dataset_candidate_register.license: dataset metadata CC-BY-4.0; the code files carry their ORIGINAL licenses (GitHub ToS apply); not uniformly permissive
dataset_candidate_register.source_code_obligations: GPL/LGPL files inside it impose obligations; GitHub ToS restricts scraping-scale redistribution
dataset_candidate_register.redistribution: prohibited at scale under GitHub ToS without API-level compliance
dataset_candidate_register.quality_security: docstring-paired functions (useful for NL-code pairs) but mixed licensing
dataset_candidate_register.verdict: useful shape, licensing too heterogeneous to use as-is

dataset_candidate_register.name: PyPI permissively-licensed packages (direct package index)
dataset_candidate_register.published_size: package count > 500k (reported); code volume ~1-2 TB raw, ~tens of billions of tokens
dataset_candidate_register.access: public index, no registration (fair-use limits apply at scrape scale)
dataset_candidate_register.license: per-package license files (majority MIT/Apache/BSD/PSF; copyleft minority must be filtered)
dataset_candidate_register.source_code_obligations: each package's LICENSE file governs; must be read and filtered at package level
dataset_candidate_register.redistribution: per-package; systematic filtering required (SPDX id + allowlist)
dataset_candidate_register.commercial_use: mostly permissive but cannot be assumed per-package without reading LICENSEs
dataset_candidate_register.quality_security: uneven quality; secret leakage common (CI tokens, keys); heavy dedup required; documentation/example code high value
dataset_candidate_register.verdict: VIABLE via the same license-gate tooling used for M3-verified; highest legal-engineering cost

dataset_candidate_register.name: RedPajama / Dolma corpora
dataset_candidate_register.languages: many incl. code (RedPajama-Data-1B has code slice), English-dominant
dataset_candidate_register.published_size: 1.2 T tokens (reported) for RedPajama-1; Dolma ~3 T
dataset_candidate_register.license: mixed CommonCrawl licenses + subset-specific licenses (e.g. C4: ODC-BY); code slice inherits GitHub licensing
dataset_candidate_register.source_code_obligations: same per-file license issue as GitHub-derived code
dataset_candidate_register.redistribution: corpus redistribution prohibited; derivative research use permitted
dataset_candidate_register.commercial_use: allowed for research under ODC-BY-1.0-style terms with attribution; code slice inherits mixed terms
dataset_candidate_register.quality_security: heavy filtering applied; still needs code-specific quality pass
dataset_candidate_register.verdict: NOT a code-first option; only if chat/general text is desired

dataset_candidate_register.name: The Pile
dataset_candidate_register.languages: many; code slice ~9% (BigCode subset, GPL-style licensing inside)
dataset_candidate_register.license: mixed: CC-BY-SA-3.0 (some slices), ArXiv (non-commercial-like terms in practice), GPL-family code slice; license indeterminate per-file
dataset_candidate_register.source_code_obligations: code slice inherits GPL/copyleft obligations; attribution and source-offer very complex
dataset_candidate_register.redistribution: practically unworkable as a redistributed corpus; research use common
dataset_candidate_register.commercial_use: generally NOT clean for commercial use of the full corpus; per-slice analysis mandatory
dataset_candidate_register.quality_security: large-scale, mixed provenance; known PII/malware content documented by authors
dataset_candidate_register.verdict: EXCLUDE for code training until per-slice review; not recommended

dataset_candidate_register.name: OASST2 (Open Assistant) instruction trees
dataset_candidate_register.source_code_obligations: share-alike applies to adapted data, not to models trained on it (per OpenRAIL-style readings), but legal review advised; code content is thin
dataset_candidate_register.redistribution: permitted with attribution, share-alike on the dataset itself
dataset_candidate_register.opt_out: implicit (contributor consent flow); small dataset, low value for code
dataset_candidate_register.quality_security: small, high-quality human data; not code-heavy
dataset_candidate_register.verdict: small CC-BY-SA general/instruction data; insufficient code mass

dataset_candidate_register.name: Databricks Dolly 15k
dataset_candidate_register.source_code_obligations: share-alike on data; code segment tiny
dataset_candidate_register.quality_security: human-authored but tiny and general; near-zero code
dataset_candidate_register.verdict: instruction-format donor only; negligible for code capability

dataset_candidate_register.name: Wiki / StackExchange dumps (general text)
dataset_candidate_register.published_size: Wikipedia ~20 GB compressed text (reported); SE ~100 GB
dataset_candidate_register.source_code_obligations: share-alike on data; code inside posts inherits mixed per-post licensing (StackOverflow CC-BY-SA-4.0 with attribution)
dataset_candidate_register.redistribution: permitted with attribution, share-alike on adapted data
dataset_candidate_register.opt_out: implicit via community conventions; large corpus, needs PII/toxicity filtering
dataset_candidate_register.quality_security: StackOverflow code is high quality; license attribution burden real
dataset_candidate_register.verdict: acceptable general-text; code volume still small relative to need

dataset_candidate_register.name: Evaluation benchmarks as training data (HumanEval / MBPP / EvalPlus / L0.2 bench)
dataset_candidate_register.official_source: openai/human-eval; google-research MBPP; evalplus; this repo
dataset_candidate_register.license: HumanEval MIT; MBPP CC-BY-4.0; EvalPlus MIT
dataset_candidate_register.quality_security: THE point: these are evaluation sets; ANY training on them destroys the measurement
dataset_candidate_register.verdict: EXCLUDED BY DESIGN AND BY PROJECT POLICY (no training on eval sets)

register_summary.policy: No candidate may enter training merely because it is publicly accessible; every candidate above requires legal sign-off before acquisition or ingestion.
